A small loop. An explicit contract.

Browser automation you can reason about.

A model proposes an action. The runtime checks the policy. A browser adapter performs the allowed step. A fresh observation tells the agent whether the task actually advanced.

That separation is the foundation: swap an adapter, inspect a decision and test a failure case without treating the whole agent as a black box.

The first milestone is this loop in Java, with testable boundaries. Browser adapters, model-provider integrations and a supervision console need to earn their place through working, verified implementations.

What is Diya Lamp?

An open-source browser-agent project written in Java. The direction is cloud-agnostic and model-agnostic: separate the runtime from provider-specific adapters, with explicit oversight of browser actions. It is in development.

What can it control?

The browser is the scope: observe web pages, propose browser actions, act within a run’s policy and verify the result. Desktop apps and shell execution are outside this project’s scope.

What can I use today?

The public repository has an experimental Java task-coordination library with transactional claims, fenced leases, checkpoints, approvals and ordered task history. A browser-agent prototype is being built on that foundation. No complete browser or model-provider integration is advertised as ready.

Can I use any model or cloud?

Provider neutrality is an architectural goal, not a claim of universal compatibility. The runtime is designed for separate model and browser adapters, with self-hosting locally or on your own cloud infrastructure. Supported adapters will be documented as they are implemented and tested.

Where will run data live?

The existing Java coordination library uses CockroachDB for task state, checkpoints, approvals and history. The browser-loop prototype uses local file snapshots; it is not connected to that SQL store yet. Replication and regional resilience depend on deployment. Browser recovery after real failures is not yet verified.

Will there be a managed service?

Yes, we plan a paid managed cloud with an advanced console for supervising browser agents. Run inspection, approval and intervention controls are planned. The hosted service, console, sign-in and pricing are not available yet.
